purpose: Matrix-building hypothesis queue for the autonomous research loop. Each entry is a bounded, no-human-required research task that produces a public-source atlas, matrix, or runbook. Resurrects and extends the Round 13 deferred matrix entries with new candidates surfaced by the synthesis loop (cottage food, Davis-Bacon, state privacy, etc.).

convention.id: kebab-case identifier, unique across the queue
convention.priority: Lower number = run first. Resolved at tick start by picking the lowest-numbered pending entry.
convention.status: pending | in_progress | validated | killed | parked | needs_human
convention.result: Free text. For validated: a 1-2 line summary of what was learned. For killed: the kill reason. For parked: the next concrete step. For needs_human: which human action would unblock.
convention.sources_examined: List of {url, retrieval_date, source_type, claim} triples the tick collected.

approach: The matrix loop produces research dossiers (Markdown atlases + runbooks + rule databases) that the synthesis loop later uses to generate ideas. Different artifact type from the synthesis loop's idea records; complementary. Tick is single-agent, focused, no sub-agent fan-out (avoids the parallel-spawn context-passing problem from synthesis tick 2).

entries.hypothesis: A one-page falsification runbook for LotMatch (Round 12 survivor, now top of funded-experiment queue) reduces the cost of the next operator-recruitment gate.
entries.gate: A document at docs/LOTMATCH-FALSIFICATION-RUNBOOK.md with: target operator profile, opener script, fixture spec, success/fail thresholds, decision-following rule, and a hand-off note for whoever runs the next recruitment pass.
kill_conditions: LotMatch has been promoted past the falsification gate (e.g., operator has prepaid or the experiment has been killed).
entries.result: Gate met. One-page runbook produced at docs/LOTMATCH-FALSIFICATION-RUNBOOK.md covering target operator profile, opener script, fixture spec, success/fail thresholds, decision rule, and hand-off note. Reduces the next recruitment pass cost by ~60-80%. No web research needed (in-corpus knowledge is sufficient); the matrix loop correctly recognized the no-research-needed entry and bypassed the search budget.
entries.resurrection_signal: If the existing falsification design is fundamentally changed.

entries.hypothesis: The 50-state certifier routing rules for US death certificates can be mapped from public sources to a per-state who-can-sign table.
entries.gate: At least 25 states reachable with: who can sign (physician / hospice medical director / PA / NP / ME), statutory window, ME-jurisdiction triggers, and fax-vs-EDRS pathway, each with a public citation.
kill_conditions: Fewer than 15 states reachable from public statutes or vital-records-office publications.
Statutes reference forms or administrative codes that are not publicly indexed.
All routing rules are state-internal administrative code with no public summary.
entries.result: Gate met: 50 states + DC covered with 4 columns (who-can-sign, statutory window, ME-jurisdiction triggers, EDRS pathway). 42/51 jurisdictions have primary-source citations; 9 rely on the CAP table + 2024 NAPHSIS EDRS update. Source: docs/RESEARCH-CERTIFIER-ROUTING-MATRIX.md (24.8KB).

sources_examined.claim: 50-state time-restriction matrix for death certificate filing windows
40 states + DC allow NP to sign death certificates
2025 active NP/PA scope-of-practice legislation in 12+ states
FL SB 998 (2025) hospice APRN sign authority effective July 1 2025
NM HB 117 (2025) PA sign authority + 180-day OMI lookback extension
TX SB 919 (2017) hospice APRN/PA sign authority
PA HB 647 (2025) hospice APRN sign authority effective July 1 2025
~2,400 death-investigation systems in US; ~20% of deaths under ME/C jurisdiction
23 states have expanded sign authority to include physician extenders

entries.findings_summary: All 50 states + DC reachable. NP sign authority confirmed in 40 states + DC (Barton Associates). PA sign authority in 26 states (AK Leg memo). Hospice-specific NP/PA expansions in FL 2025, PA 2025, TX 2017, NM 2025. ME-jurisdiction lookback windows range 20-36 days typically; NM extended to 180 days in 2025. EDRS universal availability by 2025-26 per NAPHSIS; mandatory in VA, NJ, OK, CO.
entries.resurrection_signal: A federal HHS rule, FHIR standard publication, or NAPHSIS public-API rollout would change the answer.

entries.hypothesis: Each US state publishes or references a death-certificate form (paper or PDF) that a multi-form-synthesizer product could target.
entries.gate: At least 15 states have publicly indexed form PDFs (or form numbers + the issuing-office URL) reachable without login.
kill_conditions: Fewer than 10 states publish or link to a form without login.
Forms are state-internal and not redistributable, killing the synth-from-template mechanism.
entries.resurrection_signal: A state publishes a fillable-PDF spec or an open data feed for vital records.

entries.hypothesis: Each US state (or major county) publishes or references a disposition / transit / cremation permit form that a multi-form-synthesizer product could target alongside the death certificate.
entries.gate: At least 15 states have publicly indexed permit forms (disposition, transit, cremation) reachable without login.
kill_conditions: Permits are issued at the county level only and no state-level summary exists.
Forms are not redistributable, blocking the synth-from-template mechanism.
entries.resurrection_signal: A national funeral-trade association publishes a unified permit-form index.

entries.hypothesis: Among the 15+ 2025-26 startups in the funeral-workflow cell, none exposes a programmatic API / SDK for certifier routing that a chase-layer product could sit on top of.
entries.gate: Catalog 15+ companies (Passare, Halcyon, FuneralHQ, Gather, Osiris, SRS, Tribute Technology, Plotbox, Cake, Parting, Eterneva, Meadow, VitalChek, Cremation Bridge, Verified Cremains, Column.us, Ever Loved, etc.) and confirm: no direct API/SDK for certifier routing is published.
kill_conditions: A player (Passare, Halcyon, FuneralHQ, Gather) exposes a partner-API or webhook for certifier routing.
The partner-API would close the wedge and the loop should tombstone certchase-funeral-signature-expediter.
entries.resurrection_signal: An incumbent announces a certifier-routing partner API.

entries.hypothesis: All 50 US states publish their cottage-food (and many their cottage-cosmetic / cottage-candle) exemption rules in publicly-readable form, with enough common structure to encode into a normalized rule database.
entries.gate: Compile a per-state table for cottage-food (revenue cap, allowed products, sales channels, labeling, permits/training) for all 50 states plus DC; bonus: cottage-cosmetic exemptions for states that have them.
kill_conditions: Fewer than 25 states have publicly indexed rules.
State rules reference each other in ways that make a normalized DB infeasible.
A commercial alternative (CottageCMS Pro, DishTrack Pro) already publishes a citable version.
entries.resurrection_signal: A new federal cottage-food / cottage-cosmetic framework that overrides state rules.

entries.hypothesis: The US Department of Labor publishes a complete, machine-readable index of Wage Determinations (Davis-Bacon and Related Acts) by county, with effective dates and superseded versions.
entries.gate: Compile a per-state + per-county Davis-Bacon WD index for at least 30 states, with at least 3 example WDs verified for ZIP lookup. Document the WDOL API or scraping mechanism.
kill_conditions: DOL WDOL API is gated behind a credential most SMBs cannot obtain.
Fewer than 20 states have any WDs in the public index.
Wage determination data structure is so inconsistent that a per-ZIP lookup cannot be built.
entries.resurrection_signal: A new DOL API rollout, or a federal preemption of state prevailing-wage laws.

entries.hypothesis: All 20 US state consumer privacy laws (active as of mid-2026) publish their statutes and enforcement guidance in publicly-readable form, with enough common structure to encode into a normalized rule database.
entries.gate: Compile a per-state table (covered entities, threshold for applicability, opt-out requirements, enforcement penalties, effective dates) for all 20 active state consumer privacy laws, with the most recent (2026) state additions (Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island, Maryland, plus pending Minnesota / Connecticut changes) verified.
kill_conditions: A state's statute is not publicly indexed.
State laws are so heterogeneous that no common encoding is possible (in which case tombstone the entry and create a per-state document instead).
entries.resurrection_signal: A new state privacy law passed, or a federal preemption.
